structured.answer: I'd open an account at פסגות and buy the fund the page already had picked, "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125". The page said I'd end up with about 86,045 ₪ after 10 years. That's with its default 10,000 ₪ now and 500 ₪ a month, not my own numbers.

stuck.why: The task gave no amounts, so I left 10,000 and 500. I didn't want to fight the sliders, so the 86,045 isn't for my 30,000.

stuck.where: Fund list, the -0.04% under the chosen fund and the -0.37% to -0.54% under the others (screens 7-8)
stuck.why: The minus signs scared me. Is it losing money every year? I went with the one the page had already picked because its minus was the smallest.
Took me a second to see this was the other option ending up with less, not me losing 1,030.

findings.what: Every fund shows a minus percent in big letters. It looks like they all lose money, and nothing next to it says what it means.
The result uses the page's 10,000/500 example. Nothing pushes me to put in my own amount before showing a big number.
Red minus shekel amounts (-1,030 ₪) next to each fund look like losses
Too many colours in the cost bar and the legend sits far from it
